title: Indigenous imagery policy, audit and servicing plan
subtitle: Clean 2024 audit, Elora moose sculpture, water and wastewater master plan, Riverfest Elora and firefighter toll booths
overview: Council received a draft policy on Indigenous-themed names, logos and imagery in Township facilities and directed staff to consult the public and return with a final draft. Council allocated $20,000 from the DEI Capital Project for a phased reconciliation-focused pathway, including a permanent contextual display at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre {{vote:m4}}.

Council approved the 2024 audited consolidated financial statements {{vote:m2}}. The auditor reported a clean opinion, no required corrections and no significant control deficiencies. Council also endorsed the Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan, opening a public review period before projects reach budget deliberations {{vote:m6}}.

Other approvals included a new sculpture, "Mo, the Moose Fawn", in the Elora Green Space with a $6,000 Township contribution {{vote:m5}}. The consent agenda appointed Heritage Centre Wellington members, approved two firefighter toll booth fundraisers and gave Riverfest Elora exclusive use of Bissell Park and Municipally Significant Event status {{vote:m1}}. A rezoning for 6235 Guelph Street was deferred.

decisions.detail: Council received the draft policy, directed a communication plan and final draft, and allocated $20,000 from the DEI Capital Project for the reconciliation-focused pathway.
Council approved the December 31, 2024 audited draft consolidated financial statements as presented by KPMG LLP.

decisions.item: Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan
decisions.detail: Council endorsed the plan, directed a Notice of Study Completion, and asked staff to bring plan projects forward in budget deliberations.
Council approved installing "Mo, the Moose Fawn" with a memorial plaque, a $6,000 General Capital Reserve contribution and delegated authority to sign agreements.

Council appointed Heritage Centre Wellington members, approved two firefighter toll booths, and granted Riverfest Elora exclusive Bissell Park use and Municipally Significant Event status for August 15-17.

debate: On the Indigenous imagery policy, one councillor asked whether $20,000 was enough given the education events, speakers and display, and proposed raising it to $40,000. Staff said $20,000 covers 2025 work and more can be requested in August or at budget time. The amendment was withdrawn.

A guest speaker from Haudenosaunee Lacrosse urged consultation, permission and Indigenous-created imagery, and said education builds understanding. A councillor asked about involving school boards. Staff said the focus is community and families for now.

On the servicing plan, a planning consultant for a landowner in the expanded Elora area asked for confirmation that infrastructure timing is development-driven and that alternative servicing could be considered. Staff said the plan is high-level, the Township will set development sequencing, and applications can still be submitted.

Councillors asked why plan projects start around 2030. Staff said timing depends on growth, and a large inventory of approved but unbuilt lots already exists. One councillor said empty lots should be finished first.

On the sculpture, councillors asked whether the base would resist damage and who proposed the earlier pond. The fund manager said the pond was proposed with the Township and sited by the parks department. A councillor supported the shared $6,000 cost.
